clue.text: Bewildered, did he thirst for gossip?

indicators.note: someone bewildered is thrown into confusion, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A puzzled questioner wonders whether someone was really thirsting for scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish the dirt is an informal idiom for spreading scandalous tittle-tattle about people.

clue.text: About to withdraw bill that 21 is known for?

parts.note: something disappearing is in the act of leaving, on the point of withdrawing from view
a bill passed by Parliament becomes an Act

explanation.surface: Someone is about to pull a parliamentary bill, the thing a peer is famous for.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is LORD LUCAN, the British peer who vanished in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered and was never found.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Lucan's fame rests on vanishing without trace, a real-life vanishing trick.

clue.text: String of shops alongside beauty parlour

indicators.note: String of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A row of shops stands next to a place where people get their hair and nails done.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a business offering hairdressing and cosmetic treatments, i.e. a beauty parlour.

clue.text: End trial with explosion destroying a part of plant

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters of the words before it apart, so they are rearranged
destroying says the a is wiped out of the pool of letters being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A test of some device ends in a blast that wrecks a bit of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with explosion' scrambles ENDTRIAL, and 'destroying a' removes A from that pool before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the slender coiling shoot by which a climbing plant clings to supports.

clue.text: Scrap previous wordplay raised as an example

parts.note: ex means former or previous, as in ex-wife
a pun is a play on words

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are written upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An editor drops a clever earlier bit of wordplay that was offered as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' in a down clue turns EG upwards into GE; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge something is to erase or delete it completely, to scrap it.

clue.text: Adolescent cheers up dons put in prison

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so one word wears the other inside it

parts.note: to immure someone is to shut them up within walls, to imprison them

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, a meaning of cheers

explanation.surface: A teenager applauds as university lecturers are locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but means wears or puts on; 'up' turns the British thank-you around.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescent as an adjective means not yet fully grown up, so immature in behaviour.

clue.text: 'This bed's horrid', says Violet Elizabeth, as story intensifies

indicators.note: Violet Elizabeth Bott, the lisping girl in Richmal Crompton's Just William books, says th for s

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot, and being horrid is something that sickens

explanation.surface: A spoilt little girl complains about her bed as a story gets more gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth threatens to 'scream and scream till I'm sick' in the Just William stories, with a lisp that turns 'sickens' into THICKENS; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom marks a moment when a narrative becomes more complicated and mysterious.

clue.text: Wasn't tempted to interfere — neither Jack nor Jill did

definitions.meaning: an idiom for refraining from meddling with something
in the nursery rhyme the pair went up the hill to fetch water and came down together, so neither left the well on their own

explanation.surface: Someone resisted meddling, and the nursery-rhyme pair didn't either.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving well alone means not interfering with something already satisfactory; the second reading is a playful literal sense of the words.

clue.text: Conservative HQ's prerogative?

definitions.meaning: a headquarters is a centre and a prerogative is a right, so the right belonging to the centre

explanation.surface: A query about what a Tory party headquarters is entitled to.
explanation.definitionFit: On the political spectrum, positions somewhat to the right of the middle are conservative ones.

clue.text: One Greek character left in time to find another

indicators.note: in says the letters before it sit inside the word for time

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period of time
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: One Greek letter, left long enough, will lead you to a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' is a link word; the definition 'another' means another Greek character.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, a further letter beside psi.

clue.text: High priest number two holding mass for stricken city

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the next one inside it

parts.note: the Pope is the highest priest of the Roman Catholic Church
m is the symbol for mass in physics
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A senior cleric and his deputy celebrate mass for a disaster-struck town.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town buried and destroyed by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Batting pundit ran informal game of cricket

indicators.note: batting can mean flapping or beating about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator ran between the wickets while batting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batting' belongs in the cricket picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-and-run is a casual form of cricket in which the batter must run whenever bat touches ball.

clue.text: Land cultivation hard on slope

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the preceding piece

parts.note: a tilt is a slope or slant
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Farming the ground is tough work on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilth is the tilling of soil, or the state of tilled ground, for growing crops.

clue.text: Quits flat

definitions.meaning: being quits means having settled the score

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: square with someone after repaying, and having a level surface.

clue.text: Hold tailless mammal back pretty quickly

indicators.note: tailless says the last letter of the word for hold is cut off

parts.note: to allege is to maintain or hold that something is so

indicators.note: back means the word for the animal is read in reverse

parts.note: the otter is an aquatic mammal

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a short-tailed creature and returns it fairly fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' looks attached to the mammal but trims ALLEGE to ALLEG; 'back' turns OTTER into RETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is a musical tempo marking meaning fairly brisk, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Fancy dress mostly ready-made

indicators.note: to dress something is to arrange it, so the letters are set out anew
mostly means nearly all the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A costume for a fancy-dress party bought off the peg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy dress' reads as one phrase, but 'Fancy' is the definition and 'dress' rearranges READYMAD, the clue's last word minus its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is an imagined notion, much like a reverie or idle dream.

clue.text: Sport available on large rescue vessel

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the pieces before

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
Noah's Ark saved the animals from the Flood
someone around is about and available

explanation.surface: Some recreation is on offer aboard a big lifeboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is a verb here, not a noun; 'on' places the word for available after the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport, as a verb, is to play about frivolously, which is to fool about.

clue.text: Former filling stations unopened — dedicated people sought

indicators.note: filling means the word for former goes inside the other
unopened says the first letter of the word for stations is removed

parts.note: one's station is one's position, i.e. a job
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: Old petrol stations, now closed, are wanted by devoted folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling stations' reads as petrol stations, but 'filling' is the insertion signal and 'unopened' beheads the word for stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblates are lay people dedicated to religious life, often sought as volunteers by monasteries.

clue.text: Wind resistance in middle of Channel different

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the seven-letter word
in says the resistance symbol is put inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: other means different
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Air resistance in mid-Channel is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel is the English Channel between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: A norther is a strong cold wind blowing from the north.

clue.text: Snappy greeting between clubs repeated

indicators.note: between puts the greeting inside the doubled card-suit letter

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
repeated supplies the clubs abbreviation a second time
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A curt hello passed between two golf clubs over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can mean smart and stylish, as in a snappy dresser, which is chic.

clue.text: Conduced round home, given internal protection

indicators.note: round means the word for conduced goes about the word for home

parts.note: to conduce is to lead towards a result, so conduced means led
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Something brought about safety at home, protecting from within.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat or box that is lined has an inner layer that shields it.

clue.text: Call round, unfortunately missing member of the House

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters come out in disorder

explanation.surface: A sad visit to someone, with a parliamentarian absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Lucan, a peer and so a member of the House of Lords, disappeared in 1974 and was never found.
explanation.definitionFit: As an earl, Lucan sat in the House of Lords, and he has been missing since 1974.

clue.text: Look to exploit wretch

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
to use someone is to exploit them

explanation.surface: Watch out for someone taking advantage of a poor soul.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a contemptible person, a scoundrel or wretch.

clue.text: Handiest resolute knight sent to the front

indicators.note: sent to the front says the knight's letter is moved to the start

parts.note: earnest means serious and determined, resolute
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: The most useful determined knight was dispatched to the battle line.
explanation.definitionFit: Handiest means most conveniently close by, the closest to hand.

clue.text: Arrogance of man averse to keeping uniforms apart

indicators.note: keeping means the word for the hostile man holds the letters inside
apart says the two letters for uniforms go in at separate places

parts.note: a hater is a person averse to something
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet, and the plural gives a second U

explanation.surface: A haughty man dislikes keeping regimental dress separate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniforms' gives two Us, and 'keeping … apart' puts them into HATER at separate points.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauteur is a haughty, proud manner of superiority.

clue.text: Opportunists, one waiting to open morning paper

indicators.note: to open means the waiter splits the paper's name apart by going inside

parts.note: The Times is a British daily newspaper published in the morning
a server is one who waits at table

explanation.surface: Someone waiting at table opens the morning newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-servers adapt their views to suit whoever holds power, behaving like self-serving opportunists.
